taskVersion.name: deadline-math-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Convert a published contest deadline to the reader's local time. Cases: day rollover, the weeks when the EU and US change clocks on different dates, 12 AM and AoE wording, non-hour offsets. Ground truth computed with zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On September 30, 2026, "ET" will be Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), which is UTC-4. Madrid, Spain, observes Central European Summer Time (CEST) on that date, which is UTC+2. Therefore, Madrid will be 6 hours ahead of EDT.

5:00 PM ET + 6 hours = 11:00 PM (23:00) Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima, Peru observes Peru Standard Time (PET), which is UTC-5. There is no daylight saving time in Peru.
12:00 UTC minus 5 hours is 07:00.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CEST (Central European Summer Time) is UTC+2. JST (Japan Standard Time) is UTC+9. Therefore, Tokyo is 7 hours ahead of CEST (9 - 2 = 7). Adding 7 hours to 9:00 AM CEST gives you 4:00 PM (16:00) on the same day in Tokyo.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PDT (Pacific Daylight Time) is UTC-7. In October 2026, Madrid will be observing CEST (Central European Summer Time), which is UTC+2, as Daylight Saving Time typically ends later in October. Therefore, Madrid time is 9 hours ahead of PDT. Adding 9 hours to October 11, 2026, 11:59 PM PDT, results in October 12, 2026, 08:59 AM in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PST (Pacific Standard Time) is UTC-8. Madrid, Spain, in early March, observes CET (Central European Time) which is UTC+1. Therefore, Madrid is 9 hours ahead of PST.

Adding 9 hours to March 3, 2026, 11:59 PM PST:
11:59 PM PST + 9 hours = 8:59 AM on March 4, 2026, in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET (Central European Time) is UTC+1. Los Angeles observes PST (Pacific Standard Time) in February, which is UTC-8. Therefore, Los Angeles is 9 hours behind CET (1 - (-8) = 9 hours). Subtracting 9 hours from 10:00 AM on February 2nd moves the time back to 1:00 AM on February 2nd, and then back another 9 hours means it's the previous day. So, 10:00 AM CET minus 9 hours is 01:00 AM on February 2nd, and then 10:00 AM minus 9 hours takes you to 01:00 AM *the day before*.

ANSWER: 2026-02-01 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

JST (Japan Standard Time) is UTC+9. Lima, Peru uses PET (Peru Standard Time), which is UTC-5. This means Lima is 14 hours behind JST.

Subtracting 14 hours from 8:00 AM on May 5th:
8:00 AM - 8 hours = 12:00 AM (midnight) on May 5th.
12:00 AM - 6 more hours = 6:00 PM (18:00) on May 4th.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 28, 2026, Pacific Time (PT) will be PDT (UTC-7) as Daylight Saving Time in the US ends in November. Madrid, Spain, will be on CET (UTC+1) as Daylight Saving Time in Europe ends on the last Sunday of October. Therefore, Madrid is 8 hours ahead of PT. Adding 8 hours to 11:59 PM on October 28 will push the time into the next day.

2026-10-28 23:59 PT + 8 hours = 2026-10-29 07:59

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid observes Central European Time (CET) on October 30, 2026, which is UTC+1. Eastern Time (ET) on October 30, 2026, will be Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), which is UTC-4. Therefore, Madrid is 5 hours ahead of EDT.

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 14:00

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET is UTC+1. New York will be observing Eastern Daylight Time (EDT) on October 27, 2026, which is UTC-4, as Daylight Saving Time ends in early November. Therefore, New York is 5 hours behind CET. 18:00 CET minus 5 hours is 13:00 EDT.

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is November 2, 2026, at 11:59 PM PT.
On November 2, 2026, Pacific Time (PT) will be Pacific Standard Time (PST), which is UTC-8.
On November 2, 2026, Madrid will be Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1 (Spain switches off DST on the last Sunday of October).
Therefore, Madrid is 9 hours ahead of PT (UTC+1 vs UTC-8).

Adding 9 hours to 11:59 PM on November 2nd:
11:59 PM PT + 9 hours = 8:59 AM on November 3rd in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On March 20, 2026, Pacific Time will be PDT (UTC-7) because Daylight Saving Time in the US will have started. Madrid, Spain, will still be on CET (UTC+1) as its Daylight Saving Time typically starts later in March. The difference between UTC-7 and UTC+1 is 8 hours. Adding 8 hours to 11:59 PM on March 20 will move the time and date forward.

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 07:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET (Central European Time) is UTC+1. In March 2026, Los Angeles will be observing PDT (Pacific Daylight Time), which is UTC-7. This means CET is 8 hours ahead of PDT.

12:00 PM CET - 8 hours = 4:00 AM PDT

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 04:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 12, 2026, Eastern Time (ET) will be Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), which is UTC-4. Madrid will be observing Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2. Therefore, Madrid is 6 hours ahead of EDT. Adding 6 hours to 12:00 AM ET results in 6:00 AM on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

"AoE" (Anywhere on Earth) means the deadline expires when the latest possible time zone (UTC-12) crosses that time. So, 23:59 on October 9, 2026, in UTC-12 is equivalent to 11:59 UTC on October 10, 2026. On October 10, 2026, Madrid, Spain, will be observing Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2. Adding 2 hours to 11:59 UTC gives 13:59 CEST.

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 13:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Registration closes 12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PT (Pacific Time) in August refers to PDT (Pacific Daylight Time), which is UTC-7. Madrid, Spain, in August observes CEST (Central European Summer Time), which is UTC+2.

The difference between PDT (UTC-7) and CEST (UTC+2) is 9 hours (Madrid is 9 hours ahead of PDT).

So, 12:00 PM (noon) PT on August 14, 2026, becomes 21:00 (9 PM) in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

IST (Indian Standard Time) is UTC+5:30. On November 10, 2026, Madrid will be observing CET (Central European Time), which is UTC+1. Therefore, IST is 4 hours and 30 minutes ahead of Madrid time. Subtracting 4 hours and 30 minutes from 11:59 PM (23:59) IST gives 7:29 PM (19:29) in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-11-10 19:29

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Nepal Standard Time (NPT) is UTC+5:45.
Lima, Peru observes Peru Standard Time (PET), which is UTC-5.

Nepal is 10 hours and 45 minutes ahead of Lima (5:45 - (-5) = 10:45).

To find the deadline in Lima time, subtract 10 hours and 45 minutes from the Nepal time:
April 2, 2026, 5:00 PM NPT (17:00 NPT)
17:00 - 10 hours = 7:00
7:00 - 45 minutes = 6:15

Since 17:00 is in the afternoon, subtracting 10 hours and 45 minutes does not cause the date to roll back to the previous day.

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 06:15

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 6, 2026, Adelaide will be observing Australian Central Daylight Time (ACDT), which is UTC+10:30. Madrid will be observing Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2.

The time difference means Madrid is 8 hours and 30 minutes behind Adelaide (10:30 - 2:00 = 8:30).

To find the deadline in Madrid time, subtract 8 hours and 30 minutes from 10:00 AM on October 6:
10:00 AM - 8 hours 30 minutes = 1:30 AM on October 6.

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 01:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney time on October 3, 2026, 6:00 PM means 18:00. On October 3, Sydney will be on Australian Eastern Standard Time (AEST), which is UTC+10. Madrid will be on Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2. The difference is 8 hours (10 - 2 = 8). Madrid is 8 hours behind Sydney. So, 18:00 Sydney time minus 8 hours is 10:00 Madrid time on the same date.

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 10:00
